item.title: libsoup_2_4: drop
item.description:
tracking issue: closes #360897

the 2.4 ABI of libsoup has long been unsupported upstream, and security issues have popped up since then in code on the libsoup 3.0 ABI branch (and been fixed there, but not for 2.4). this has been known in nixpkgs since late 2024, and #427813 marked the package vulnerable in july 2025 (over a full release cycle ago). the large majority of consumers have migrated off. (for further information on migration efforts in nixpkgs, see the tracking issue and backlinks within it.) given this, we think its about time to propose a complete drop of the package.

this pr is a mix of marking the remaining dependents broken and dropping them entirely. most of these are fairly straightforward, and for details, see my triage comment on the tracking issue (https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/360897#issuecomment-4581564223) and the individual commit messages. there are only two packages we're unsure about:

  • hqplayerd: hqplayer 5.x has a hard dependency on gupnp (1.4), gssdp (1.4), and an old version of rygel, all of which depend on libsoup 2.4. however, upstream just recently published hqplayer 6.x, which supposedly has a "New in-house implementation of UPnP 2.0 AV software stack to remove Rygel dependency", which sounds to me like we might be able to drop hqplayerd.rygel and the gupnp dependency with a 6.0 update. we attempted this, but were not able to figure it out (because it's an opaque binary download and we're not familiar with the subject matter). we've opted to mark it broken in the hopes that this can be migrated in the future. cc maintainer: @lovesegfault
  • citrix_workspace{,_25_08_10,_26_01_0}: this is, again, a wrapped binary with unclear dependencies. libsoup 2.4 seems to be hard-required though, as auto-patchelf shouts if it's not provided. we are unsure, however, of what the impacts would be if this were to be forcibly removed. from what we can tell, this does not appear to be in any other distros either, so we can't take inspiration from anywhere else. this one seems the most unfortunate, as it appears to have both an active upstream and active interest within nixpkgs (there have been recent prs with fixes and such). we're not really sure what to do about this one. we've opted to mark it broken, but we would very much appreciate other thoughts. cc maintainer: @flacks

other than those two, everything else here is fairly straightforward. we believe this is fine, but iunno, we'll see. would happily welcome any other thoughts on anything.
